{{short description|German soprano|bot=PearBOT 5}} {{Infobox person | name = Diana Damrau | image = File:Diana Damra, Sopran (17162764382) (cropped).jpg | caption = Damrau in 2012 | image_upright = 1.2 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1971|5|31|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Günzburg]], Bavaria, [[West Germany]] | alma mater = [[Hochschule für Musik Würzburg]] | occupation = Opera singer ([[soprano]]) | years_active = 1995–present | title = [[Kammersänger]]in | awards = [[Bavarian Maximilian Order for Science and Art]]
[[Bavarian Order of Merit]] | spouse = {{marriage|[[Nicolas Testé]]|2010}} | children = 2 | website = {{URL|https://diana-damrau.com/en/|diana-damrau.com}} }} '''Diana Damrau''' ({{IPA|de|diːˈana ˈdamʁaʊ|lang}}; born 31 May 1971) is a German [[soprano]] who has achieved international fame for her performances, primarily in opera, but also in concert and lieder. She has been successful in [[coloratura soprano]] roles since her early career, and gradually proceeded into heavier roles of the 19th-century Italian bel canto repertoire. Her signature roles include the Queen of the Night in ''[[The Magic Flute]]'', Zerbinetta in ''[[Ariadne auf Naxos]]'', Lucia in ''[[Lucia di Lammermoor]]'', and Violetta in ''[[La traviata]]''. Educated at the [[Hochschule für Musik Würzburg]], she had been engaged at the opera companies in Würzburg, Mannheim, and Frankfurt. Since beginning her freelance career in 2002, she has been performing on leading stages frequently, such as the [[Bavarian State Opera]], [[Vienna State Opera]], and [[Metropolitan Opera]], where she appeared in 12 consecutive seasons since her debut in 2005/06. She also leads concert performances with French bass-baritone [[Nicolas Testé]], whom she married in 2010. Damrau has recorded dozens of opera and lieder recital albums since signing to EMI/[[Virgin Classics]] (absorbed into Warner/[[Erato Records]] in 2013). She was invested as Bavarian Kammersängerin and has been awarded the [[Bavarian Maximilian Order for Science and Art]] and the [[Bavarian Order of Merit]]. ==Early life== Damrau was born in [[Günzburg]], Bavaria on 31 May 1971. She was inspired to become an opera singer after watching [[Zeffirelli]]'s [[La Traviata (1983 film)|1983 film of ''La traviata'']], which featured [[Plácido Domingo]] and [[Teresa Stratas]].{{cite news |title=Halte Wien unbedingt die Treue! |work=Wiener Zeitung |date=2006-08-10 |access-date=2021-01-19 |url=https://www.wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/kultur/klassik/283822_Halte-Wien-unbedingt-die-Treue.html}} She began her operatic studies with {{ill|Carmen Hanganu|de}} at the [[Hochschule für Musik Würzburg]]. During her studies, she developed an [[edema]] on a vocal cord.{{cite news |url=http://www.augsburger-allgemeine.de/politik/Diana-Damrau-Weltstar-Mutter-Managerin-id17594011.html |title=Diana Damrau: Weltstar, Mutter, Managerin |trans-title=Diana Damrau: Star, mother, manager |type=Interview |work=[[Augsburger Allgemeine]] |date=2011-11-18 |lang=de |first=Holger |last=Sabinsky-Wolf}}{{cite news |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/muenchen/article1487837/Diana-Damrau-ein-Weltstar-aus-Schwaben.html |title=Diana Damrau, ein Weltstar aus Schwaben |work=[[Die Welt]] |date=2007-12-22 |first=Martina |last=Kausch |trans-title=Diana Damrau, a world star from Swabia}} After consulting with several doctors, she decided to undergo an [[Alternative medicine|alternative therapy]] without surgery. The treatment lasted about one and a half years.{{cite news|url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/kultur/boing-fliegt-mir-die-krone-runter/5753754.html |title=Boing, fliegt mir die Krone runter |work=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] |type=Interview |access-date=2015-01-17 |lang=de |first=Marie |last=von Baumbach}} After graduating from music conservatory she worked in Salzburg with [[Hanna Ludwig]]. ==Career== === Early career, debuts, coloratura soprano roles === Damrau made her operatic debut in 1995 as Barbarina in ''[[The Marriage of Figaro]]'' at the [[Mainfranken Theater Würzburg]]. In the next two years, she was engaged at the same theatre, featuring as Eliza Doolittle in ''[[My Fair Lady]],'' and then as the Queen of the Night in Mozart's ''[[The Magic Flute]],'' her debut in that role, and in the world premiere of [[Salieri]]'s ''Cublai, gran kan de' Tartari'' (1998).{{Cite episode|title=Mad About Music: Diana Damrau|series=Mad About Music|network=WQXR-FM|date=2007-12-02|url=https://www.wqxr.org/story/47094-diana-damrau/?tab=transcript}} Next, she performed with the [[Mannheim National Theatre]] and [[Oper Frankfurt]] for two years each. She made her [[Bavarian State Opera]] debut in 1999 with Zerbinetta in ''[[Ariadne auf Naxos]]'', and her [[Vienna State Opera]] debut with the Queen of the Night in 2000.{{cite web |url=http://www.klassik-heute.de/4daction/www_interpret?id=2919 |title=Diana Damrau: Biographie, Diskographie |website=Klassik Heute |access-date=2021-03-13 |lang=de}} In 2001, she made her [[Salzburg Festival]] debut, portraying the Naiad alongside [[Natalie Dessay]]'s Zerbinetta; she became a regular in Salzburg and returned in the subsequent six editions. Since 2002, she embarked a freelance career, and had frequent engagements with the Bavarian State Opera in roles such as Adele in ''[[Die Fledermaus]]'', Marzelline in ''[[Fidelio]]'', and the Queen of the Night. She took part in the world premiere of [[Friedrich Cerha|Cehra]]'s ''Der Riese vom Steinfeld'' in the role of Small Woman in Vienna.{{cite news |url=https://www.welt.de/print-welt/article394814/Grotesker-Kreuzweg-Der-Riese-vom-Steinfeld.html |title=Grotesker Kreuzweg: "Der Riese vom Steinfeld" |date=2002-06-17 |first=Ulrich |last=Weinzierl |work=Die Welt |access-date=2020-12-26}} Her engagements in Salzburg consist exclusively of roles in Mozart operas: ''The Magic Flute'' (Queen of the Night, 2002), ''[[Die Entführung aus dem Serail]]'' (Blonde, 2003; Konstanze, 2004), ''The Marriage of Figaro'' (Susanna, 2007).{{cite news |title=Die technischen Tricks des Zauberflötenreich-Zirkus |url=https://www.wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/kultur/klassik/181099_Die-technischen-Tricks-des-Zauberfloetenreich-Zirkus.html |date=2002-07-31 |work=Wiener Zeitung |trans-title=The technical tricks of the Magic Flute Empire Circus |access-date=2019-08-15}}{{cite news |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/kultur/im-anfang-war-der-zweifel/434978.html |title=Im Anfang war der Zweifel |date=2003-07-29 |work=Der Tagesspiegel |first=Frederik |last=Hanssen |access-date=2020-12-26}} In the 2006 edition, which celebrated Mozart's 200th anniversary, she played the Queen of the Night in the premiere of [[Pierre Audi]]'s production of ''The Magic Flute'', and Fauno in ''[[Ascanio in Alba]]''.{{cite news |url=https://www.wienerzeitung.at/nachrichten/kultur/klassik/283758_Die-Zauberfloete-zweiter-Start.html |title=Die Zauberflöte, zweiter Start |date=2006-08-01 |work=Wiener Zeitung}}{{cite news |work=Wiener Zeitung |url=https://www.wienerzeitung.at/startseite/archiv/113464_Mit-der-Scheibtruhe-zum-Hochzeitsfest-gekarrt.html |title=Mit der Scheibtruhe zum Hochzeitsfest gekarrt |date=2006-08-05}} Damrau made her [[Royal Opera, London]] debut in January 2003, in [[David McVicar]]'s new production of ''The Magic Flute'',{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/die-zauberflote-royal-opera-house-london-131343.html |title=Review: Die Zauberflöte, Royal Opera House |date=2003-01-20 |work=The Independent|first=Edward|last=Seckerson|author-link=Edward Seckerson}} {{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2003/jan/27/classicalmusicandopera.artsfeatures |title=Die Zauberflöte, Royal Opera House, London |date=2003-01-27 |work=The Guardian |first=Tim |last=Ashley}} and then appeared in ''[[Arabella]]'' (Fiakermilli), ''Ariadne auf Naxos'' (Zerbinetta), and the world premiere of Maazel's ''[[1984 (opera)|1984]]'' in two consecutive seasons.{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2004/may/24/classicalmusicandopera |title=Arabella, Royal Opera House, London |date=2004-05-24 |work=The Guardian |first=Andrew |last=Clements}}{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/06/24/arts/a-svelte-soprano-pleases-but-fans-play-down-size.html |title=A Svelte Soprano Pleases, but Fans Play Down Size |date=2004-06-24 |work=The New York Times |first=Sarah |last=Lyall}}{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2005/may/04/classicalmusicandopera1 |title=1984, Royal Opera House, London |date=2005-05-04 |work=The Guardian |first=Andrew |last=Clements}} At the [[Opera Frankfurt]], she sang her first Konstanze in ''Die Entführung'', a role she then repeated in Munich and Salzburg. In March 2004, she sang the role of Zdenka in ''Arabella'' for the first time in Munich.{{cite press release |title=Diana Damrau singt in "Arablla" und die "Entführung aus dem Serail" an der Bayerischen Staatsoper |url=https://www.staatsoper.de/presse/presseinformationen/presse-infos-oper/mitteilung/news/diana-damrau-singt-in-arabella-und-die-entfuehrung-aus-dem-serail-an-der-bayerischen-staatsoper.html?no_cache=1&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&cHash=58b4bdf585fa5effb005764883f949f4 |date=2004-03-24 |access-date=2021-01-04 |publisher=Bavarian State Opera}} In December 2004, she was invited to sing the title role in Salieri's ''[[Europa riconosciuta]],'' conducted by [[Riccardo Muti]], for the reopening of [[La Scala]] in Milan.{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/europa-riconosciuta-la-scala-milan-679902.html |title=Europa Riconosciuta, La Scala, Milan |date=2004-12-04 |first=Peter |last=Popham |work=The Independent |access-date=2019-08-15}} In 2005, she portrayed Gilda in the premiere of [[Doris Dörrie]]'s controversial production of ''[[Rigoletto]]'' in Munich,{{cite news |url=https://rp-online.de/kultur/opernskandal-von-doris-doerrie_aid-17187231 |title="Rigoletto" in München: Opernskandal von Doris Dörrie |date=2005-02-22 |work=Rheinische Post |agency=afp}} and later in the year, made her [[Metropolitan Opera]] debut in New York City in the role of Zerbinetta.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/09/18/arts/music/ill-see-your-high-g-and-raise-you-an-a-flat.html |title=I'll See Your High G and Raise You an A Flat |date=2005-09-18 |first=Matthew |last=Gurewitsch |work=The New York Times |access-date=2020-12-26}} === Transition, more lyric soprano and bel canto roles === Damrau sang her first Susanna in ''[[The Marriage of Figaro]]'' in February 2006 at La Scala,{{cite news |title=Luz de Strehler, luz de Mozart |date=2006-02-10 |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2006/02/10/espectaculos/1139526007_850215.html |first=Juan Ángel |last=Vela del Campo}} and subsequently in Vienna. Apart from Konstanze in a new production co-produced with the [[Burgtheater]],{{cite news |title=Gefühlsnahkampf im Serail |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2432742/gefuehlsnahkampf-im-serail |date=2006-05-03 |work=Der Standard |first=Ljubisa |last=Tosic}} she had been featured at the [[Vienna State Opera]] in three consecutive seasons with several other roles.{{Cite web|title=Vorstellungen mit Diana Damrau|url=https://archiv.wiener-staatsoper.at/search/person/3525|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-07|website=Vienna State Opera|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007092216/https://archiv.wiener-staatsoper.at/search/person/3525 |archive-date=2021-10-07 }} Since her debut in the 2005/06 season, she appeared in consecutive seasons at the Met, where she starred in new productions of ''[[The Barber of Seville]]'' (Rosina, 2006), ''[[Die ägyptische Helena]]'' (Aithra, 2007), and Rossini's comic opera ''[[Le comte Ory]]'' (Countess Adèle, 2011),{{cite web |url=https://theclassicalreview.com/2011/03/the-met-serves-up-a-sexy-inspired-cast-in-delightfully-theatrical-le-comte-ory/ |title=The Met serves up a sexy, inspired cast in delightfully theatrical "Le Comte Ory" |date=2011-03-25 |first=Corinna |last=da Fonseca-Wollheim |website=The Classical Review}} besides revivals of ''Die Enführung aus dem Serail'', ''Lucia di Lammermoor'' (role debut as Lucia), ''La fille du régiment'', ''Rigoletto'', and ''[[L'elisir d'amore]].'' She made Metropolitan Opera history in the 2007/08 season by appearing as both Pamina and the Queen of the Night in different performances of ''[[The Magic Flute]]'' in the same run, after which she retired from playing the Queen,{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/28/arts/music/28midg.html |title=One Voice for Innocence and Experience |date=2007-10-28 |work=The New York Times|first=Anne|last=Midgette|author-link=Anne Midgette|access-date=2019-08-15}} a role that she had sung in more than 15 productions. She made guest appearances at the [[Teatro Real]] (Zerbinetta), [[Semperoper]] in Dresden (Gilda), [[Theater an der Wien]] (Pamina), [[Festspielhaus Baden-Baden]] (Sophie in ''[[Der Rosenkavalier]]''). She continued to be associated with the [[Bavarian State Opera]], with performances including a new production of ''[[Ariadne auf Naxos]]'' in 2008. In the 2008/09 season she returned to [[Royal Opera, London]] for Gretel in ''[[Hansel and Gretel (opera)|Hänsel und Gretel]]'' and Adina in ''[[L'elisir d'amore]]''. The 2009/10 season saw her Rosina and role debut in the title role in ''[[Manon]]'' (Vienna State Opera), role debuts of Marie in ''[[La fille du régiment]]'' ([[San Francisco Opera]]) and Donna Anna in ''[[Don Giovanni]]'' ([[Grand Théâtre de Genève]]),{{cite news |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2009/10/14/review-virtuoso-peruvian-tenor-juan-diego-florez-and-german-soprano-diana-damrau-wowed-audience-at-s-f-opera/ |title=Virtuoso Peruvian tenor Juan Diego Flórez and German soprano Diana Damrau wowed audience at S.F. Opera |date=2009-10-14 |first=Richard |last=Scheinin |work=The Mercury News}}{{cite news |url=https://www.nzz.ch/die_verpasste_deutung-1.4179979 |title=Die verpasste Deutung |date=2009-12-14 |work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |first=Thomas |last=Schacher}} and her last Konstanze at the Liceu, in the 2003 [[Christof Loy]] production she premiered.{{cite news|last=Barranco|first=Justo|date=2010-08-13|title=El rapto de Diana Damrau|work=La Vanguardia|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/cultura/20100413/53905499217/el-rapto-de-diana-damrau.html}} Damrau has furthered her exploration of the [[bel canto]] repertoire with highlights including role debut in Elvira in ''[[I puritani]]'' in Geneva in January 2011,{{cite news |url=https://www.forumopera.com/spectacle/damrau-ne-convainc-pas |title=I Puritani - Genève |date=2011-01-29 |work=Forumopera.com}} and the title role in Donizetti's ''[[Linda di Chamounix]]'' at the [[Liceu]].{{cite web |title=Barcelona Rarity: Damrau and Flórez can't Salvage Linda di Chamounix |url=http://seenandheard-international.com/2012/01/lindadichamounix_barcelona_donizetti_damrau_florez_jmirurzun_jensflaurson/ |date=2012-01-03 |website=Seen and Heard International |first=José M. |last=Irurzun}} She has since brought her portrayal in Donizetti's ''[[Lucia di Lammermoor]]'' to Berlin and Vienna. She premiered in a new production of Strauss' ''[[Die schweigsame Frau]]'' at the 2010 [[Munich Opera Festival]], and portrayed all four heroines in Offenbach's ''[[The Tales of Hoffmann]]'' in a new production at the Bavarian State Opera premiered in October 2011.{{cite news |url=https://www.merkur.de/kultur/marathonfrau-mm-1462387.html |title=Bayerische Staatsoper: Diana Damrau singt in "Hoffmanns Erzählungen" vier Rollen |date=2011-10-25 |first=Markus |last=Thiel |work=Münchner Merkur}} In May 2012, she returned to Geneva for Philine in Ambroise Thomas' ''[[Mignon]]''. Following the birth of her second child in autumn 2012, Damrau returned to the stage with a new production of Verdi's ''[[Rigoletto]]'' at the Metropolitan Opera in February 2013; this was followed by her role debut in the title role of Verdi's ''[[La traviata]]'' in the same house. In October 2013, she sang in the world premiere of [[Iain Bell]]'s ''[[A Harlot's Progress (opera)|A Harlot's Progress]]'' at the [[Theater an der Wien]].{{cite news |url=https://www.welt.de/kultur/buehne-konzert/article121141115/Maedchen-die-fallen-und-Maedchen-die-schiessen.html |title=Mädchen, die fallen, und Mädchen, die schießen |date=2013-10-23 |first=Manuel |last=Brug |work=Die Welt}} In March 2014 she sang in ''[[La sonnambula]]'' at the Metropolitan Opera. She debuted in the role of Countess d'Almaviva in the new production of ''[[The Marriage of Figaro]]'' at [[La Scala]], which premiered on 26 October 2016.{{cite web |url=http://www.teatroallascala.org/en/season/2015-2016/opera/le-nozze-di-figaro.html |title=''Le nozze di Figaro'' (''The Marriage of Figaro'') |website=La Scala |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924073945/http://www.teatroallascala.org/en/season/2015-2016/opera/le-nozze-di-figaro.html |archive-date=2019-09-24}} She took up the title role in ''[[Maria Stuarda]]'' at the [[Zürich Opera House]] in April 2018.{{cite news |url=https://www.nzz.ch/feuilleton/in-maria-stuarda-kommt-es-zum-streit-zweier-koeniginnen-und-zweier-sopranistinnen-ld.1375602 |title=In ''Maria Stuarda'' kommt es zum Streit zweier Königinnen – und zweier Sopranistinnen |date=2018-04-09 |work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |first=Thomas |last=Schacher |trans-title=In "Maria Stuarda" there is a quarrel between two queens - and two sopranos}} In 2019 she debuted as Ophélie in ''[[Hamlet (opera)|Hamlet]]'' in concert performances at the [[Liceu]] and later at the [[Deutsche Oper Berlin]].{{cite web |url=https://seenandheard-international.com/2019/03/an-outstanding-cast-leads-the-liceus-revival-of-hamlet/ |title=An Outstanding Cast Leads the Liceu's Revival of ''Hamlet''|date=2019-03-08 |first=José M. |last=Irurzun |website=Seen and Heard International}}{{citation |url=https://onlinemerker.com/berlin-deutsche-oper-hamlet-konzertante-premiere-mit-florian-sempey-in-der-titelpartie-und-diana-damrau-als-ophelie/ |title=Berlin/ Deutsche Oper: ''Hamlet''|date=2019-06-25 |website=Online Merker |first=Ingobert |last=Waltenberger |lang=de}} === Concert career === As well as performing in operas, Damrau is a regular on the concert stage. She performed alongside [[Plácido Domingo]] at the concert program "3 Orchester und Stars" in Munich to mark the opening of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]].{{cite web |title=Placido Domingo und Diana Damrau als Opernstars bei "3 Orchester und Stars" |url=https://www.ganz-muenchen.de/artculture/2006/06_juni/open_air/3_orchester_und_stars/placido_domingo_diana_damrau.html |date=2006-06-06 |website=ganz-muenchen.de}} She has performed [[lied]]er at Vienna's [[Musikverein]], [[Carnegie Hall]], [[Wigmore Hall]], La Scala, the [[Schubertiade]] in [[Schwarzenberg, Austria|Schwarzenberg]], the [[Kissinger Sommer]] and both the Munich and Salzburg Festivals, especially with [[Xavier de Maistre (harpist)|Xavier de Maistre]] as her accompanist. Her concert repertoire includes Mozart's ''[[Great Mass in C minor]]'', ''[[Requiem (Mozart)|Requiem]]'' and ''[[Exsultate, jubilate]]'' as well as Handel's ''[[Messiah (Handel)|Messiah]]''. She has performed with conductors as [[James Levine]], [[Zubin Mehta]], [[Lorin Maazel]], Sir [[Colin Davis]], [[Christoph von Dohnányi]], [[Leonard Slatkin]], [[Pierre Boulez]], [[Nikolaus Harnoncourt]] and [[Jesús López Cobos]]. ==Personal life== Damrau married French bass-baritone [[Nicolas Testé]] in May 2010.{{cite news |url=https://www.augsburger-allgemeine.de/guenzburg/Neue-Rolle-Diana-Damrau-als-Mutter-und-Ehefrau-id8114581.html |title=Neue Rolle: Diana Damrau als Mutter und Ehefrau |date=2010-07-08 |first=Helmut |last=Kircher |work=Augsburger Allgemeine}} They have two sons: Alexander, born in 2010 or 2011, and Colyn, born in 2012.{{Cite web |title=‘La Traviata’ Soprano Diana Damrau On Motherhood, Future Projects, Singing Dream Role Debut at Met Opera - Diana Damrau - Soprano |url=https://diana-damrau.com/en/2013/03/11/la-traviata-soprano-diana-damrau-on-motherhood-future-projects-singing-dream-role-debut-at-met-opera/ |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=diana-damrau.com}}{{Cite web |last=Catton |first=Pia |date=12 March 2013 |title=A Soprano Brings Her Home To Work With Her |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887324735304578356421276221906 |website=Wall Street Journal |language=English}} == Key performances == * [[La Scala]]: ''Europa riconosciuta''* (Europa), ''[[The Marriage of Figaro]]'' (Susanna), ''La traviata''* (Violetta), ''Lucia di Lammermoor'' (Lucia) * [[Metropolitan Opera]]: ''[[La sonnambula]]'' (Amina), ''La traviata'' (Violetta), ''The Magic Opera]], Munich: ''Les contes d'Hoffmann''* (Olympia/Antonia/Giulietta/Stella), ''Die schweigsame Frau''* (Aminta), ''The Magic Flute'' (Queen of the Night), ''Die Entführung aus dem Serail''* The official {{MoMP|33034|naming citation}} was published by the [[Minor Planet Center]] on 9 January 2020 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 120069}}). ==Discography== Early recordings include [[Giuseppe Verdi|Verdi]]'s [[canzoni]], Mahler's ''[[Des Knaben Wunderhorn (Mahler)|Des Knaben Wunderhorn]]'', and Schumann's ''[[Myrthen]]'', Op. 25, with the Telos label and live recordings of her summer 2005 ''Liederabend'' at the Salzburg Festival and her summer 2006 ''Liederabend'' at the Schubertiade are released on the [[Orfeo (record label)|Orfeo label]]. Damrau also appears on [[Deutsche Harmonia Mundi]]'s release of Mozart's ''[[Zaide]]'' in the title role, and performs in the trio finale from Richard Strauss' ''[[Der Rosenkavalier]]'' alongside [[Adrianne Pieczonka]] on [[Elīna Garanča]]'s first solo release with [[Deutsche Grammophon]]. Since 2007 Damrau has had an exclusive recording contract with [[EMI]]/Virgin. * ''Arie di Bravura'', her first release (2007) is a recital of Mozart, [[Vincenzo Righini|Righini]] and Salieri arias; Le Cercle de l'Harmonie, [[Jérémie Rhorer]]. * ''Donna: Opera and Concert Arias by Mozart'' (November 2008) is a collection of Mozart opera and concert arias; Rhorer and Le Cercle de l'Harmonie. * ''Coloraturas'' (November 2009). [[Munich Radio Orchestra]], [[Dan Ettinger]]. * ''Poesie: Richard Strauss Lieder'' (January 2011) is a collection of [[Richard Strauss]]' orchestral songs; [[Munich Philharmonic]], [[Christian Thielemann]]. * ''Liszt Lieder'' (October 2011) is a collection of classical songs by Liszt, accompanied by pianist [[Helmut Deutsch]]. * ''Forever'' (2013) is a collection of operetta and musical theatre numbers; [[Royal Liverpool Philharmonic]], [[David Charles Abell]]. * ''Fiamma del belcanto'' (2015) is a collection of belcanto compositions by [[Vincenzo Bellini|Bellini]], [[Gaetano Donizetti|Donizetti]], [[Giuseppe Verdi|Verdi]], [[Giacomo Puccini|Puccini]] and [[Ruggero Leoncavallo|Leoncavallo]]; recorded with the Orchestra [[Teatro Regio (Turin)|Teatro Regio Torino]], [[Gianandrea Noseda]]. * ''Meyerbeer: Grand Opera'' (2017) is a recording of pieces by [[Giacomo Meyerbeer]]; Orchestre de l'[[Opéra National de Lyon]], [[Emmanuel Villaume]]. *''Robert Schumann: Myrthen Op. 25'' (2018).
